item.title: Walnut Hill VFD hosts 56th annual fish fry Saturday

item.content:encoded:
The Walnut Hill Volunteer Fire Department is firing up the fryers this Saturday for its 56th Annual Fish Fry, running from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at the fire department.

The community event is a longtime tradition in North Escambia, offering fresh-cooked seafood and family-friendly activities while supporting the local volunteer fire department. It's a chance to grab a meal and help fund the department's operations and equipment.

If you're planning to attend, head out to Walnut Hill on Saturday between 11 a.m. and 2 p.m.

item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Jesse Guardado, 64, was executed by lethal injection Thursday evening at Florida State Prison for the 2004 murder of a Panhandle woman. According to the Department of Corrections, Guardado was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. Guardado had been convicted in connection with the death of a woman who had assisted him after his release from jail. The case…
item.content:encoded:
Jesse Guardado, 64, was executed by lethal injection Thursday evening at Florida State Prison for the 2004 murder of a Panhandle woman. According to the Department of Corrections, Guardado was pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m.

Guardado had been convicted in connection with the death of a woman who had assisted him after his release from jail. The case stems from events in 2004, more than two decades before the execution carried out this week.

The execution marks another completion of Florida's capital punishment cases, which have been carried out at a higher pace in recent years under the state's current administration.

Eligible applicants can get assistance paying electric, natural gas, and water bills, as well as reconnection fees. The program is also helping people secure…
item.content:encoded:
The Community Action Program Committee will set up at Century Town Hall on Friday from 9:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. to help North Escambia residents struggling with bills and recovery costs.

Eligible applicants can get assistance paying electric, natural gas, and water bills, as well as reconnection fees. The program is also helping people secure temporary housing after recent storm damage.

No appointment is necessary. Residents should bring documentation of income and proof of residency, along with utility bills or other evidence of the expenses they need help covering.

item.title: Clear Weekend Ahead for Pensacola Area; Temps Dipping to Low 40s
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A pleasant and chilly weekend is setting up for the Pensacola area, with clear skies and lower humidity taking hold through Sunday. Overnight lows will drop into the low 40s Saturday and Sunday night — a notable shift from earlier in the week. Friday will see increasing clouds during the day with a high near 75 degrees and light north winds at 5…
item.content:encoded:
A pleasant and chilly weekend is setting up for the Pensacola area, with clear skies and lower humidity taking hold through Sunday. Overnight lows will drop into the low 40s Saturday and Sunday night — a notable shift from earlier in the week.

Friday will see increasing clouds during the day with a high near 75 degrees and light north winds at 5 to 10 mph. Friday evening will start out cloudy but clear gradually as the night progresses, with lows bottoming out around 52.

If you're planning outdoor activities over the weekend, conditions should be ideal. Bundle up for early morning and evening hours, particularly Sunday night when temperatures will be at their lowest.

item.content:encoded:
Two North Escambia elementary schools are hosting fall festivals and carnivals today, offering families games, food, and carnival activities.

Byrneville Elementary School, located at 1600 Byrneville Road, will run its annual Fall Festival from 4 to 7 p.m. The event features games, food vendors, a hayride, mechanical bull, haunted house, carnival rides, rock climbing, and an annual basket auction.

Jim Allen Elementary is also hosting its carnival today, though specific times and details for that location were not provided in the available information. Both events offer traditional fall festival fare and are free or low-cost entertainment options for families in the North Escambia area.

item.content:encoded: An Escambia County jury has found Antonio Marshone DeSoto guilty of second-degree murder in connection with the fatal shooting of Charles Black on Main Street in McDavid last February. The jury reached its verdict Thursday afternoon after deliberating for just under two hours. DeSoto, 27, was charged in the death that occurred in the unincorporated North Escambia community. The conviction marks the resolution of a case that has been pending since the 2025 incident.

item.title: Flomaton Police Chief Justin Hetrick Resigns, Mayor Denies Department Closure
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The announcement came as Mayor Arthur Odom moved to reassure residents about the department's future. Odom publicly denied…
item.content:encoded: Flomaton Police Chief Justin Hetrick has announced his resignation, submitting his official letter on Monday, Nov. 2, with his final day set for Friday, Nov. 13, according to a Flomaton Police Department Facebook post. The announcement came as Mayor Arthur Odom moved to reassure residents about the department's future. Odom publicly denied circulating rumors that the Flomaton Police Department would close following Hetrick's departure, emphasizing that the agency remains fully operational. Hetrick's resignation comes during a period of apparent concern in the community, though no specific reason for his departure has been made public.

item.title: NAS Pensacola Homecoming Air Show kicks off Friday with free admission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The 2026 Naval Air Station Pensacola Homecoming Air Show begins Friday and continues through Saturday, offering free general admission to what's traditionally one of the region's largest annual events. The two-day show is expected to draw more than 250,000 spectators to the base. This year's air show, themed "200 Years Forged Here," celebrates NAS…
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Naval Air Station Pensacola Homecoming Air Show begins Friday and continues through Saturday, offering free general admission to what's traditionally one of the region's largest annual events. The two-day show is expected to draw more than 250,000 spectators to the base.

This year's air show, themed "200 Years Forged Here," celebrates NAS Pensacola's bicentennial milestone. The installation has been a cornerstone of naval aviation training and operations since its founding two centuries ago.

The event typically features military aircraft demonstrations, flyovers, and static displays. Attendees should plan for significant traffic and arrive early, particularly on opening day. Parking and shuttle information will be available at the gate.

item.title: Blue Angels ready for homecoming airshow after missing 2025
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Blue Angels are returning to Pensacola this weekend for their season-closing Homecoming Airshow, bringing high-octane flying demonstrations to Naval Air Station Pensacola on Friday and Saturday after last year's event was canceled. Commandeering Officer and Flight Leader Adam Bryan told WKRG News 5 that the homecoming represents a major…
item.content:encoded:
The Blue Angels are returning to Pensacola this weekend for their season-closing Homecoming Airshow, bringing high-octane flying demonstrations to Naval Air Station Pensacola on Friday and Saturday after last year's event was canceled.

Commandeering Officer and Flight Leader Adam Bryan told WKRG News 5 that the homecoming represents a major milestone for the team. "We mark this as our proverbial Super Bowl," Bryan said, underscoring the significance of ending the flying season in front of their home crowd.

The airshow marks the culmination of the Blue Angels' 2026 performance season and gives the precision flying team a chance to reconnect with the Pensacola community that has long supported their operations at NAS Pensacola.

item.title: Blue Angels return to NAS Pensacola for 200th anniversary shows this weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are set to perform at Naval Air Station Pensacola this Friday and Saturday as part of the base's 200th anniversary celebration, according to WKRG-TV 5. The high-speed demonstration team will mark the return of the iconic six-plane formation after a 2025 government shutdown forced the cancellation of previously scheduled…
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Navy Blue Angels are set to perform at Naval Air Station Pensacola this Friday and Saturday as part of the base's 200th anniversary celebration, according to WKRG-TV 5. The high-speed demonstration team will mark the return of the iconic six-plane formation after a 2025 government shutdown forced the cancellation of previously scheduled performances.

The flyovers are expected to draw crowds to the Pensacola area as residents and military families gather to witness the precision aerobatic team. The Blue Angels are among the most recognizable symbols of naval aviation and typically draw significant attendance whenever they perform in the region.

This marks a significant milestone for NAS Pensacola, which has been home to naval aviation training and operations for two centuries. The base remains one of the largest employers in the Escambia County area and continues to play a central role in Navy pilot training and fleet operations.

item.title: NAS Pensacola draws 3,000 students for STEAM career event

item.description: Naval Air Station Pensacola hosted its second annual STEAM career education event Thursday, drawing about 3,000 students from across the region. The day-long program introduced attendees to opportunities in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, according to WKRG News 5. The event brought together students with military and…
item.content:encoded:
Naval Air Station Pensacola hosted its second annual STEAM career education event Thursday, drawing about 3,000 students from across the region. The day-long program introduced attendees to opportunities in science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics, according to WKRG News 5.

The event brought together students with military and civilian professionals working in STEAM fields, giving young people a chance to explore potential career paths while learning about the diverse roles available within the naval aviation community and beyond. Thursday's gathering represented a significant expansion of what organizers described as their second year hosting the initiative at the base.

item.title: Crestview to Host America 250 Grand Parade Saturday with Olympic Medalist as Grand Marshal
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Okaloosa County America 250 Commission is inviting the public to a historic parade celebration this Saturday, November 7, at 11 a.m. along Main Street in downtown Crestview. The event marks 250 years of American independence and is expected to draw one of the largest patriotic crowds in the county's history. The parade will feature vibrant…
item.content:encoded:
The Okaloosa County America 250 Commission is inviting the public to a historic parade celebration this Saturday, November 7, at 11 a.m. along Main Street in downtown Crestview. The event marks 250 years of American independence and is expected to draw one of the largest patriotic crowds in the county's history.

The parade will feature vibrant floats, marching bands, tributes to veterans, and participation from community organizations and cultural groups. Crestview native and Olympic speed skater Mia Manganello, who won a bronze medal for the United States at the February 2026 Winter Games in Milan, Italy, will serve as the parade's Grand Marshal. Organizers encourage attendees to wear red, white, and blue or period colonial attire.

The parade will be live-streamed on Facebook at facebook.com/okaloosacountyamerica250 and on YouTube at youtube.com/@EmeraldCoastTV for those unable to attend in person. If weather forces a cancellation, a makeup date has been scheduled for Sunday, November 8, at 2 p.m.

item.title: Surfin' Santa Parade Set for Dec. 6 on Pensacola Beach
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is calling for parade entries ahead of this year's Surfin' Santa Beach Parade, a holiday tradition that draws thousands of families to the island. The parade is scheduled for Sunday, December 6, beginning at 2 p.m. from Avenida 10 and running down Via de Luna toward Casino Beach, ending at the Gulfside…
item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce is calling for parade entries ahead of this year's Surfin' Santa Beach Parade, a holiday tradition that draws thousands of families to the island.

The parade is scheduled for Sunday, December 6, beginning at 2 p.m. from Avenida 10 and running down Via de Luna toward Casino Beach, ending at the Gulfside Pavilion. Entry is open to local businesses, nonprofits, community organizations, and groups of friends. Registration fees are $50 for nonprofits and $100 for commercial businesses, with all fees nonrefundable.

Participants should check in and line up starting at 12:30 p.m. at the basketball courts (corner of Panferio Drive and Via de Luna Drive). Organizers will award prizes for the top three best-decorated floats.

Registration is now open through the Pensacola Beach Chamber of Commerce. More details are available on the chamber's website.

item.title: Pensacola Habitat for Humanity breaks ground on 9-home project at former Malcolm Yonge site
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola Habitat for Humanity will hold a groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday, November 10, at 10 a.m. for a nine-home affordable housing development on the former Malcolm Yonge Gymnasium property at 925 East Jackson Street. The project, developed in partnership with the City of Pensacola, aims to expand homeownership opportunities for residents who…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola Habitat for Humanity will hold a groundbreaking ceremony Tuesday, November 10, at 10 a.m. for a nine-home affordable housing development on the former Malcolm Yonge Gymnasium property at 925 East Jackson Street.

The project, developed in partnership with the City of Pensacola, aims to expand homeownership opportunities for residents who might otherwise struggle to afford a home in the area. The homes will be part of the Northwest Florida Community Land Trust, a structure designed to keep housing affordable for future generations of buyers.

Leaders from Pensacola Habitat for Humanity and city officials will speak at the ceremony about the vision for the neighborhood and provide additional details about the development. The organization is inviting the public and media to attend and help spread word about the opportunity to prospective homebuyers in the community.

item.title: Okaloosa County Sheriff warns of scam impersonating deputies
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to a fraud scheme in which scammers are posing as law enforcement officials, including the chief deputy, to trick people out of money or information. While specific details about how the scam operates weren't immediately available, the sheriff's office is urging residents to be cautious…
item.content:encoded:
The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office is alerting residents to a fraud scheme in which scammers are posing as law enforcement officials, including the chief deputy, to trick people out of money or information.

While specific details about how the scam operates weren't immediately available, the sheriff's office is urging residents to be cautious about unsolicited calls or contacts claiming to be from their agency. Officials remind the public that legitimate law enforcement will not solicit money over the phone or demand payment for fines or legal issues through unconventional means.

If you receive a suspicious call claiming to be from the Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office, hang up and contact the agency directly using a phone number you know to be legitimate. You can also report suspected scams to local law enforcement or the Florida Attorney General's office.

item.title: 111 Years Ago: Pensacola Bay Witnessed First Catapult Launch from Moving Ship
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: On this day in 1915, Pensacola Bay was the scene of a historic first in naval aviation. Lieutenant Commander Henry C. Mustin successfully launched an AB-2 seaplane from the armored cruiser USS North Carolina using a catapult while the ship was underway — a milestone that would shape the future of carrier-based aviation. The achievement marked a…
item.content:encoded:
On this day in 1915, Pensacola Bay was the scene of a historic first in naval aviation. Lieutenant Commander Henry C. Mustin successfully launched an AB-2 seaplane from the armored cruiser USS North Carolina using a catapult while the ship was underway — a milestone that would shape the future of carrier-based aviation.

The achievement marked a turning point in how the Navy could deploy aircraft at sea, moving beyond stationary launches from docked vessels. Mustin's flight from the USS North Carolina in Pensacola Bay demonstrated that aircraft could be rapidly launched during active operations, a capability that would become fundamental to modern naval warfare.

The feat reflects Pensacola's deep roots in naval aviation history. The area around NAS Pensacola has long been central to the development of carrier operations and aircraft launch systems that remain in use today.

item.title: ECUA Customer Service Closed Nov. 11 for Veterans Day
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority will close its Customer Service Department on Wednesday, November 11, in observance of Veterans Day, the utility announced Thursday. All other ECUA departments and offices will remain open during normal business hours. The closure will not affect residential or commercial sanitation collection schedules, which…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority will close its Customer Service Department on Wednesday, November 11, in observance of Veterans Day, the utility announced Thursday.

All other ECUA departments and offices will remain open during normal business hours. The closure will not affect residential or commercial sanitation collection schedules, which will continue on their regular routes.

Customers who need to reach ECUA during the closure can contact the utility on the following business day or through alternative service channels.
